name: TTS-WebUI

database.label: No database; settings and generated audio are plain files in the project folder

resourceFootprint.notes: Measured on 2026-10-22 (version v1.5.2 plus a few commits) in a Proxmox LXC (6 vCPU, 12 GB RAM) with an RTX 3090 passed through. The web UI idles at about 0.5 GB of RAM and about 2.2 GB after loading the Kokoro model. Generating an 8-second English sentence with Kokoro-82M took about 1.7 seconds and used about 1.2 GB of VRAM. Larger models (Bark, XTTS, Chatterbox) need more VRAM and RAM. The installation with its extensions is large: about 22 GB for the project folder in our LXC, so plan for 60 GB of disk or more. The first Kokoro run also downloaded a small language package automatically.

dockerComposeSnippet:
# TTS-WebUI is installed with its own one-click installer (see the repo README),
# not Docker. We run it natively in an LXC as a systemd service (our real unit).
# /etc/systemd/system/tts-webui.service
[Unit]
Description=TTS-WebUI
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=simple
WorkingDirectory=/root/TTS-WebUI
# A tmpfs /tmp is too small for model installs, so point TMPDIR at disk.
Environment=TMPDIR=/root/tmpdir
ExecStart=/root/TTS-WebUI/installer_files/mamba/micromamba run -p /root/TTS-WebUI/installer_files/env python server.py --docker
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=10

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
descriptionEn: TTS-WebUI is one web interface for many open text-to-speech and audio models. You can pick Kokoro for fast, light English speech, Chatterbox or XTTS for voice cloning, Bark for expressive audio and more, then generate speech from your own text entirely on your own GPU. It has a simple React interface and a larger Gradio interface with extensions, a pipeline builder, speech-to-text, audio and music tools and an outputs browser. Everything runs locally, so your text and any reference voices stay on your network. Use voice cloning only with your own voice or with clear permission.
taglineEn: One local web interface for many text-to-speech and voice models.
seoTitleEn: TTS-WebUI: self-hosted text-to-speech with Kokoro, XTTS and more — HomelabDeck
seoDescriptionEn: TTS-WebUI is a local web UI for many open TTS models such as Kokoro, Chatterbox and Bark. Real RTX 3090 numbers (about 1.7 s for an 8 s clip, 1.2 GB VRAM), a systemd unit and screenshots from our own LXC.
useCasesEn: Turning articles or notes into spoken audio with fast models such as Kokoro.
Comparing several open text-to-speech models side by side in one interface.
Cloning your own voice with models such as XTTS or Chatterbox for narration.
Generating short sound effects or music with the included audio models.
caveatsEn: An NVIDIA GPU is strongly recommended. Many models are very slow or do not run at all on CPU.
The install with extensions is large, so plan for tens of gigabytes of disk.
Each model has its own license. Check it before using the output commercially.
Only clone voices you have permission to use.
